html:
The Wounded Knee Massacre was the killing of some 250 to 300 Lakota by United States soldiers at Wounded Knee Creek on the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota, on 29 December 1890. It is often taken as the end of the wars on the Great Plains.

In 1890 the Ghost Dance spread among the Lakota on their shrunken reservations. Officials feared it as a rising. On 15 December police killed Sitting Bull at Standing Rock. The Miniconjou leader Spotted Elk, also called Big Foot, then led his band toward Pine Ridge. The 7th Cavalry stopped them and camped them at Wounded Knee.

As the soldiers disarmed the men, a shot went off, and the troops opened fire, including with rapid-firing Hotchkiss guns. Many of the dead were women and children, some hunted down as they fled. About 25 soldiers also died, many probably from their own side's fire. Twenty soldiers were given the Medal of Honor.

For the Sioux it remains a wound. In 1973 activists, many of them Oglala, occupied Wounded Knee for 71 days to protest broken treaties.
